scope: First nine provisional scene slots P0-P2; critical Input and nonforced first Output
rules: R exposure is not necessarily needed_R comprehension; classify what changes outcome.
F1 existence in docs is not evidence of reachable reverse lookup or complete inflected forms.
F1 translation can support early communication; do not require exact morphological generation or correct grammar.
Non-essential comprehension and optional clarification must never be manufactured as compulsory friction.
For counterfactual tests vary one meaningful German fact while preserving plausible action choices.
No pass status implies player learning or verified UI implementation.

cases.required_meaning: Greeting is socially meaningful but directly copying Hallo cannot prove independent learning.
cases.context_requirement: Lena waves and says Hallo; UI only says respond to greeting, not the target German word.
cases.acceptance: Accept Hallo, Hallo Lena, another clear greeting; do not require grammatical sentence.

cases.required_meaning: A0 must distinguish Schlüssel from another visible item when interpreting Nimm den Schlüssel.
cases.context_requirement: Two contrasting objects; no highlight of the correct target, no Russian object label; F1 must support both forms.
cases.acceptance: Swap the named target in a counterfactual; correct physical selection must change. Taking the other object must be repairable.

cases.required_meaning: Request to repeat is useful only when the player does not understand. An optional action must not block progress.
cases.context_requirement: NPC instruction can be repeated on request; button/help gives access to the phrase without auto-filling a reply.
cases.acceptance: Test both routes: player understands and proceeds without P3; player uses Noch einmal bitte / Ich verstehe nicht and gets a repeat.

cases.required_meaning: Arzt appears on an undirected sign; player must discover question wording without having previously read Wo in R.
cases.context_requirement: F1 supports searching a Russian meaning such as 'где' as well as looking up German Arzt, and displays usable short forms.
cases.acceptance: Test A0 with empty prior knowledge: the player can ask Wo Arzt? or similar; answer in R5 comes after the question, not before.

cases.required_meaning: Nein/nicht dort is potentially bypassed by following an unambiguous pointing animation, so motion alone is not proof of German.
cases.context_requirement: At least two plausible routes and non-spoiling contextual support; F1 contains nicht and hier/dort.
cases.acceptance: Changing nicht should alter the safe interpretation; if visuals alone determine the route, relabel this contact as contextual, not necessary.

cases.required_meaning: Bist du müde? can be read with F1 but the player must have an in-world basis to report a condition.
cases.context_requirement: Visible/explicit player condition available without a Russian menu that directly dictates 'müde'.
cases.acceptance: Accept short Ich müde, Ich bin müde, or unambiguous negation if the game condition allows it. Do not demand a fixed medical state without evidence.

cases.required_meaning: Hast du Schmerzen? introduces an abstract symptom; F1 alone may help decode but a negative answer must be grounded in state.
cases.context_requirement: The scene supports no-pain observations; alternatives are not silently ruled out by design.
cases.acceptance: Test yes/no symptom contrasts and clarify when ambiguous. If pain is impossible to know, do not claim that negative P proves comprehension.

cases.required_meaning: Wasser vs Brot must be chosen because of a genuine need; repeating Wasser after NPC is not sufficient proof of retention.
cases.context_requirement: Two visible, distinguishable supplies; the player wants drinking water; UI does not name the German answer.
cases.acceptance: Wrong object or bare Bitte must not deliver water; Wasser bitte or an equivalent short request works.

cases.required_meaning: Die Lampe ist kaputt conflicts with visible local evidence; the NPC report and panel must not pre-write the correction.
cases.context_requirement: Lamp observed lit, contrary to an explicitly labeled false or stale panel record; F1 makes nicht/kaputt discoverable.
cases.acceptance: Negative meaning changes the report: Lamp kaputt vs nicht kaputt cannot both be accepted for the same observed state.

cases.required_meaning: The target object is stated without its location; P1 asks Wo..., and the location is given only afterward.
cases.context_requirement: F1 provides way to express Wo and Lampe; scene includes distinguishable locations, no UI waypoint answering automatically.
cases.acceptance: Compare player asking for location with merely naming Lampe. R4 supplies 'im Zimmer' only after P1.

cases.required_meaning: Left/right and locked door can be bypassed by seeing a physically shut door, so a safe route alone cannot demonstrate comprehension.
cases.context_requirement: Both routes are plausible before the dialogue; R4 explicitly disambiguates after a question; no auto-highlight.
cases.acceptance: Try counterfactual layout (if the safe exit is right, text and outcome change) and check R4 comprehension, not just whether player follows an open passage.

cases.required_meaning: Where the Lagerverwalter is must not be known before P2; the long compound may require explicit F1 lookup.
cases.context_requirement: R5 mentions role, P2 asks where, R6 gives Lager; signposting does not show one highlighted destination.
cases.acceptance: Actor ownership and site must be distinguished; learner can ask Wo Lagerverwalter? and follow understood location.

cases.required_meaning: Lena knows only her red light; player knows local green. Text-only dialogue 'Hörst du mich?' must not silently require spoken comprehension.
cases.context_requirement: Two panels with non-shared readings; communication channel is textual and clearly presented, no audio-only content.
cases.acceptance: Check that player conveys their own local green status; copied red remote status is wrong. Verify the odd audio-language line remains just incidental.

cases.required_meaning: Inventoried 3, 1 broken, 2 usable: a correct request cannot be derived solely from an obvious click target or a Russian instruction.
cases.context_requirement: Stock labels and quantity have clear contrast; F1 numbers and Zustand; actual need for two working lamps established.
cases.acceptance: With a different damage count, the correct usable count changes, and the requested quantity must remain player-driven.
